study.title: Matthew 28 Resurrection, sending and the presence of Jesus
study.overview: Matthew 28 concludes the gospel with the empty tomb, the confirmation of the resurrection, the attempt to discredit the fact and commission of Jesus to the disciples. The chapter highlights that the resurrection is not only a triumph over death, but the foundation of the church's mission: Jesus, now recognized as the holder of all authority, sends his to make disciples among all nations and promises his continuous presence to the end.

outline.title: The empty tomb and the intervention of the sky
outline.explanation: Women go to the tomb at dawn and find signs that something decisive has happened. The earthquake, the angel, and the fear of the guards show that the resurrection is not a common event, but a direct action of God that overcomes human attempts to keep Jesus shut up in death.

outline.title: The proclamation of the resurrection and the encounter with Jesus
outline.explanation: The angel interprets the empty tomb, declares that Jesus rose and sends the women to the disciples. On the way, Jesus himself finds them, receives worship and confirms that the disciples must go to Galilee, showing that the resurrection generates witness, joy and obedience.

outline.title: The fake version to hide the fact
outline.explanation: The guards report the incident, and the religious leaders organize an alternative explanation by bribery. The text exposes a conscious opposition to the truth: instead of investigating, they prefer to fabricate a narrative to protect one's own position.

outline.title: The final commission of Jesus
outline.explanation: In Galilee, the eleven worship Jesus, although some still doubt. He declares his universal authority and sends the disciples to make disciples, baptizing and teaching to obey all that he commanded, with the promise of his continued presence.

study.context: The chapter mentions the main groups linked to the drama of passion and resurrection: the disciples women, the guards, the chief priests, the elders and the eleven disciples. The account also highlights Galilee as a place of reunion, according to the instruction given by Jesus. The notes received indicate that the women's testimony reinforces the historical credibility of the report and that the accusation of body theft was plausible in the ancient world, which helps to understand why the lie was considered verossimilar to many.
study.theology: Matthew 28 presents the resurrection as confirmation that Jesus is the living Lord and cannot be restrained by death, human authorities or false narratives. The worship of the disciples before the risen Jesus shows that the correct answer to his victory is reverence and submission. When he declares to have received all authority in heaven and on earth, the church's mission ceases to be human initiative and becomes a response to the lordship of Christ. The mandate to make disciples includes baptizing in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, which points to an explicitly Trinitarian faith. It is also clear that discipleship is not only an initial decision, but a continuous learning of obeying the commandments of Jesus. The promise of permanent presence closes the gospel with comfort: the risen Christ accompanies his church in mission.

scholarViews.insight: The mention of two women as witnesses increases the historical credibility of the account, because an inventor of stories would hardly choose women as principal witnesses in a culture in which his testimony was seen as less reliable.
Jesus sends the disciples to teach to observe all that he commanded, and the promise to be with them every day shows that the Christian mission depends on the constant presence of Christ himself.

questions: How does the resurrection of Jesus change the way you view fear, suffering, and apparent defeat?
In which areas do you run the risk of listening to a convenient version of the truth, rather than responding in faith to the biblical testimony?
What does it mean, in practice, to make disciples not only converts, but people taught to obey all that Jesus commanded?
study.practice: This week, set aside time to reread Jesus" commandments in Matthew chapters 5 to 7 and identify a concrete obedience that you need to practice. Then pray for courage to witness to Christ clearly, without fear of rejection, remembering that the mission is sustained by his authority and presence. If you already believe, think of a person to whom you can encourage in faith with words and attitudes that point to the living Christ.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided are limited and do not detail questions of chronology, exact location of the hill, nor explain in depth the doubt of some disciples in verse 17. Nor is it possible to affirm, from these notes, more than the general meaning of baptism in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit and the promise of the continuous presence of Jesus.
